status: prospective active covariance audit locked before evaluation outcomes; finite-support controller study, not learned-LLM evidence
research_question: Can trusted-label queries targeted by verifier-score geometry detect harmful verifier optimization more label-efficiently than passive policy sampling?
development_seed_policy: thresholds were chosen from separate exploratory seeds 0-399; evaluation uses disjoint seeds 20000-21023 and must not be changed after outcomes

verifier_geometry.construction: same fixed-norm verifier-error geometry used by the prospective equal-KL mechanism experiment

active_proposal: r_i proportional to p_i * abs(v_i - E_p[v]); passive control uses r_i=p_i
estimator: importance-weighted mean of y_i*(v_i-E_p[v]) with y in [0,1]; exact proxy scores and baseline policy are free, only y labels are counted
confidence_interval: two-sided Hoeffding interval using the exact distribution-free range of the single-sample importance estimator

primary.prediction: on harmful rho=-0.75 tasks at n=256, active block rate >=0.75 while passive block rate <=0.10; active wrong-sign decisive rate <=0.02 and active mean estimator range is strictly smaller

secondary_reporting: all budgets and both arms; decisive/block/allow rates, wrong-sign decisive rate, interval radius, estimator range width and importance coefficient
theory: for a_i=v_i-E_p[v], minimizing max_i |p_i a_i/r_i| over proposal distributions yields r_i proportional to p_i|a_i|; this reduces worst-case concentration width without using trusted labels
scope: finite-support active-auditing proof of concept with exact policy and proxy scores; no claim that this is optimal for learned LLM verifiers, correlated labels, or production traffic
